title: Manhattan Incident and Silent Coup Consolidate Army Rule
note: June 1951 naval officers seized Phibun aboard the US dredge Manhattan, army/air force bombed the vessel, Phibun swam ashore, and navy power was fatally weakened. November 1951 silent coup (abolishing the 1949 constitution) also confirmed.

title: Anti-Communist Activities Act Criminalises Dissent
note: The Anti-Communist Act was passed on 13 November 1952 following the failed 1952 Peace Rebellion; used broadly to suppress dissent and labour activists, consistent with the description.

title: Thailand Signs Manila Pact, Joins SEATO as Founding Member
note: Thailand was a founding signatory of the Southeast Asia Collective Defence Treaty signed in Manila in September 1954; SEATO headquarters was in Bangkok.

title: Sarit Thanarat Coup Ousts Phibun, Inaugurates Military Developmental State
note: Sarit staged the coup on 16 September 1957 ousting Phibun; a second coup in October 1958 abolished the constitution. All core facts confirmed.

title: First National Economic Development Plan Launched with World Bank
note: Thailand's First National Economic Development Plan (1961–1966) was prepared with World Bank guidance starting around 1959; NESDB was created to coordinate planning.

title: Southern Malay-Muslim Insurgency Begins in Border Provinces
note: The southern insurgency in Pattani, Yala, and Narathiwat intensified in the early 1960s driven by Thai assimilationist policies; year 1960 is consistent with sourcing the early phase.

title: Communist Party of Thailand Launches Armed Insurgency
note: The CPT formally launched armed insurgency in 1961 in the rural northeast with Maoist tactics and Chinese support; confirmed by Wikipedia on Communist Party of Thailand.

title: Thanat-Rusk Communique Formalises Bilateral US Security Pledge
note: The Thanat–Rusk communiqué was signed in March 1962 by Thai FM Thanat Khoman and US Secretary of State Dean Rusk, affirming individual US defense commitment to Thailand.

title: Thai Troops Deployed to Vietnam – Queen's Cobras Commit to US War
note: Thailand sent troops beginning 1965; the Queen's Cobras (~2,000) were followed by the Black Panthers (~10,800); the ~11,000 peak figure in the event conflates both units but total Thai commitment was ~40,000 over the war. Minor numeric imprecision, core facts correct.

title: Bangkok Declaration Establishes ASEAN with Thailand as Co-Founder
note: ASEAN was founded on 8 August 1967 with the Bangkok Declaration signed by Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, and Singapore; Thai FM Thanat Khoman was a key founding figure.

title: New Constitution Restores Partial Civilian Government Under Thanom
note: Thanom promulgated a new constitution in 1968 with a bicameral parliament and appointed Senate; elections in 1969 followed with Thanom remaining PM. Core facts confirmed.

title: Thanom Self-Coup Abolishes Constitution and Bans Political Parties
note: Thanom staged a self-coup in November 1971, annulling the 1968 constitution, dissolving parliament, and banning political parties; the triumvirate ruled through the National Executive Council.

title: October 14 Uprising Topples Military Triumvirate
note: Uprising on 14 October 1973 killed 77 (not 'at least 77' as stated — confirmed 77 deaths) and King Bhumibol facilitated the triumvirate's departure. Minor wording discrepancy only.

title: People's Constitution Promulgated – Most Liberal Charter in Thai History
note: A democratic constitution was promulgated in October 1974 by a constituent assembly providing for a fully elected parliament and extensive civil liberties; set the stage for 1975 elections.

title: Thailand Normalises Relations with China, Ending Decades of Isolation
note: PM Kukrit Pramoj visited Beijing in July 1975 establishing full diplomatic relations with the PRC; China subsequently ended support for the CPT.

title: Communist Indochina Victories Create Domino Alarm in Bangkok
note: Fall of Saigon and Phnom Penh in April 1975 and Pathet Lao takeover in December 1975 created strategic anxiety in Bangkok; students fled to CPT camps. All facts confirmed.

title: October 6 Massacre and Military Coup End Democratic Experiment
note: On 6 October 1976, rightwing paramilitaries and police attacked Thammasat University; official toll was 46 killed, unofficial estimates exceed 100. Military coup followed the same day.

title: Vietnam Invades Cambodia, Creating Security Crisis on Thailand's Border
note: Vietnam invaded Cambodia in December 1978 creating a major security crisis on Thailand's border; Bangkok coordinated with China and the US to support Khmer resistance. All facts confirmed.

title: General Prem Tinsulanonda Takes Power – Eight Years of Semi-Democracy
note: Prem assumed the premiership in February 1980 after Kriangsak resigned; his government lasted until 1988 and he survived two coup attempts with royal backing. All facts confirmed.

title: CPT Insurgency Collapses Under Amnesty Policy and Chinese Withdrawal
note: Prem's amnesty combined with China ending support after the Sino-Vietnamese split accelerated the CPT collapse; the insurgency was effectively over by the early 1980s. Confirmed.

title: Young Turks Coup Attempt Fails After Royal Endorsement of Prem
note: In April 1981 (April Fools' Day), Class 7 'Young Turks' staged a coup; Prem fled to Nakhon Ratchasima with the Royal Family, and the king's support caused the coup to collapse within days.

title: Baht Devaluation Corrects Trade Deficit, Sets Stage for Export Boom
note: Thailand devalued the baht in 1984 to address a trade deficit; the adjustment stabilised the economy and set the stage for the export-led manufacturing boom of the late 1980s.

title: Plaza Accord Triggers Wave of Japanese Manufacturing Investment
note: The 1985 Plaza Accord drove yen appreciation, prompting Japanese manufacturers to relocate to Thailand; electronics, automotive, and textile factories multiplied on the eastern seaboard.

title: Chatichai Wins Election – First Elected PM in Over a Decade
note: Chatichai led Chart Thai to victory in July 1988, becoming Thailand's first elected PM in over a decade; pledged to turn Indochina into a marketplace. All facts confirmed.

title: Economic Boom Reaches Tiger Economy Levels
note: Thailand's GDP grew over 10% annually in 1988–1989, earning tiger economy comparisons; manufacturing exports and FDI hit record levels. Confirmed.

title: Military Coup Ousts Chatichai on Corruption Grounds
note: On 23 February 1991, the NPKC staged the coup against Chatichai on corruption grounds ('Buffet Cabinet'); Anand Panyarachun appointed interim PM. All facts confirmed.

title: Black May Massacre Triggers King's Intervention and Democratic Restoration
note: 52–100 killed in May 1992 protests; King Bhumibol summoned Suchinda and Chamlong on 20 May; Suchinda resigned; Democrat-led civilian government under Chuan followed. All confirmed.

title: Thailand's 100 Percent Condom Programme Becomes Global AIDS Model
note: The 100% Condom Programme became national policy in August 1991 (not 1993); pilot began in 1989. The event year is off by at least 2 years. International recognition grew from 1991 onwards, with formal WHO/UNAIDS validation by 1996.

title: BIBF Capital Account Liberalisation Creates Structural Currency Mismatch
note: BIBF licenses were granted by the first Chuan Leekpai government in 1993, not 1994. The year is off by one year.

title: Baht Collapse Triggers Asian Financial Crisis
note: Thailand floated the baht on 2 July 1997, triggering the Asian financial crisis; baht lost over 50% of its value and GDP contracted ~10% in 1998. All core facts confirmed.

title: IMF Rescue Package – $17.2 Billion with Austerity Conditions
note: IMF unveiled a rescue package of more than $17 billion on 11 August 1997; required fiscal austerity and closure of finance companies. The $17.2B figure is consistent with Wikipedia's 'more than $17 billion.'

title: People's Constitution – Most Democratic Charter in Thai History
note: Promulgated 11 October 1997; drafted by a directly elected constituent assembly; introduced elected Senate, Constitutional Court, and anti-corruption bodies. Called the 'People's Constitution.' All facts confirmed.

title: Thaksin Shinawatra Founds Thai Rak Thai, Reshaping Electoral Politics
note: Thaksin founded Thai Rak Thai in 1998 (officially registered July 1998); the event year of 1999 is slightly off but within the 1998–1999 founding/organisation period. Minor discrepancy.

title: Thaksin Wins Landslide – Thai Rak Thai Takes 248 Seats
note: Thai Rak Thai won 248 of 500 seats in January 2001 election; formed government with coalition reaching 325 seats. The 248 seat count is confirmed.

title: 30-Baht Universal Healthcare Scheme Launched
note: Universal coverage reforms introduced in 2001 and the 30-baht scheme formally launched in 2002; event covers both years, consistent with Wikipedia.

title: War on Drugs – Over 2,500 Extrajudicial Killings in 90 Days
note: War on drugs launched 14 January 2003; 2,275 killed in first 3 months per Human Rights Watch, over 2,500 total. Fact-finding panel found more than half had no drug links. All core claims confirmed.

title: Southern Insurgency Escalates – Krue Se Mosque and Tak Bai Incidents
note: Krue Se Mosque stormed April 2004 (32 militants killed confirmed); Tak Bai incident October 2004 resulted in 78–85 detainee deaths from suffocation. Event says '85 detainees' vs confirmed 78; minor discrepancy.

title: Indian Ocean Tsunami Kills 5,400 on Thailand's Andaman Coast
note: Tsunami on 26 December 2004 killed ~5,400 in Thailand; Khao Lak had 3,950 confirmed deaths (unofficial ~4,500); Phi Phi Island and Phuket also hit. All core facts confirmed.

title: Thaksin Wins Unprecedented Outright Parliamentary Majority
note: Thai Rak Thai won 377 of 500 seats on 6 February 2005, the first single-party outright majority in Thai history. Yellow Shirt movement also emerged in 2005. All facts confirmed.

title: Shin Corp Sale and Yellow Shirts Trigger September 19 Military Coup
note: Shinawatra family sold Shin Corp stake to Temasek on 23 January 2006 for 73 billion baht; coup staged 19 September 2006 while Thaksin was at UN in New York. All core facts confirmed.

title: Military-Drafted Constitution Approved in Restricted Referendum
note: Military-drafted constitution approved August 2007 referendum with 57% support; campaigning against it was restricted. Contains provisions limiting elected governments through unelected bodies.

title: Yellow Shirts Occupy Airports; Constitutional Court Dissolves Pro-Thaksin Parties
note: PAD occupied Suvarnabhumi and Don Mueang airports November 2008; Constitutional Court dissolved People's Power Party and two coalition partners in December; Abhisit became PM. All facts confirmed.

title: Global Financial Crisis Contracts Thai Economy
note: Thailand's export-dependent economy contracted approximately 2.3% in 2009 amid the global financial crisis; recovery began by late 2009 as Asian demand recovered. Plausible and consistent with sources.

title: Red Shirt Crackdown Kills 91 in Bangkok – Ratchaprasong Occupation
note: Red Shirts occupied Ratchaprasong from April to May 2010; Wikipedia gives 'more than 85 killed' vs event's 'at least 91' — minor numeric discrepancy; nearly 2,000 injured confirmed. Core facts match.

title: Yingluck Shinawatra Elected – First Female Prime Minister
note: Pheu Thai won 265 seats in July 2011; Yingluck became Thailand's first female prime minister. All facts confirmed.

title: Catastrophic Floods Cause $46.5 Billion in Losses, Disrupt Global Supply Chains
note: 2011 floods killed 815, affected 13.6 million people; World Bank estimated 1.425 trillion baht (US$46.5 billion) in economic losses; industrial estates in Ayutthaya and Pathum Thani submerged. All facts confirmed.

title: PDRC Protests Paralyse Bangkok, Setting Stage for 2014 Coup
note: PDRC protests began October 2013 after collapse of Yingluck's amnesty bill; Suthep demanded appointed people's council; February 2014 snap election annulled by Constitutional Court. All confirmed.

title: Prayuth Chan-ocha Stages Coup, Establishes NCPO Junta
note: Prayuth staged coup on 22 May 2014 establishing the NCPO; suspended constitution, declared martial law, used Section 44 absolute powers. Described as twelfth coup since 1932. All facts confirmed.

title: Erawan Shrine Bombing Kills 20 in Central Bangkok
note: Bomb exploded at Erawan Shrine on 17 August 2015 killing 20 and injuring 125 (event says 'more than 120'); suspects with Turkish passports linked to networks affected by Uyghur deportations. All core facts confirmed.

title: Military Charter Approved in Restricted Referendum with Appointed Senate
note: Referendum passed in August 2016 with 61% support; campaigning against was criminalised; includes 5-year fully appointed Senate with PM selection powers. All facts confirmed.

title: King Bhumibol Dies After 70-Year Reign – Era of Stabilising Monarchy Ends
note: King Bhumibol died 13 October 2016 aged 88 after 70 years and 126 days on the throne; decisive political interventions in 1973, 1981, 1992 confirmed. Year-long mourning period followed.

title: King Vajiralongkorn Proclaimed Rama X, Amends Constitution for Royal Powers
note: Vajiralongkorn formally accepted the throne 1 December 2016; requested constitutional amendments giving expanded royal powers without a regent; parliament approved changes in January 2017. Event year 2017 is when the 2017 constitution was promulgated with these amendments.

title: Tham Luang Cave Rescue – International Operation Saves 13 Trapped
note: 12 boys and their coach trapped in Tham Luang cave in Chiang Rai from 23 June 2018; all 13 rescued by 10 July in an international operation. All facts confirmed.

title: Eastern Economic Corridor Launched to Attract High-Technology Investment
note: EEC launched in 2018 as a flagship initiative for advanced manufacturing, aerospace, and digital industries; built on eastern seaboard industrial zones. All facts confirmed.

title: Disputed Election Returns Prayuth Despite Opposition Popular Majority
note: March 2019 elections saw pro-democracy parties win more popular votes but Prayuth returned via the 250 appointed senators and electoral formula; Future Forward won 81 seats then was dissolved. All confirmed.

title: Future Forward Dissolved – Youth Protests Demand Monarchy Reform
note: Future Forward dissolved 21 February 2020 for fiscal impropriety (illegal loan from its leader); triggered massive youth protests in 2020–2021 making unprecedented monarchy reform demands. All facts confirmed.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Collapses Tourism, GDP Contracts 6.1 Percent
note: Tourism virtually disappeared in 2020; IMF estimated GDP contraction of 6.7% (event says 6.1%); 2019 arrivals were ~39.8 million not 'over 50 million' as stated. Minor numeric discrepancies but core facts correct.

title: Lèse-Majesté Prosecutions Multiply – Over 200 Cases Against Activists
note: Over 200 lèse-majesté cases filed between 2020 and 2022 against protest leaders and students; penalties of 3–15 years per count; Thailand among most intensive users of monarchical defamation law. Confirmed.

title: Move Forward Wins Election but Is Blocked from Government by Senate
note: Move Forward won 151 seats (most of any party) in May 2023; Pita blocked by military-appointed Senate; Pheu Thai formed government with pro-military parties; Srettha Thavisin elected PM on 22 August 2023. All facts confirmed.

title: Thaksin Returns from Exile After 15 Years, Begins Prison Term
note: Thaksin returned to Thailand on 22 August 2023 ending 15 years of exile; taken into custody to begin 8-year sentence (reduced to 1 year by royal commutation); widespread perception of a political deal. All core facts confirmed.

title: Move Forward Dissolved; Paetongtarn Shinawatra Becomes PM
note: Constitutional Court dissolved Move Forward on 7 August 2024 over lèse-majesté reform campaign; Srettha removed on ethics grounds; Paetongtarn sworn in 18 August 2024 as youngest premier. All facts confirmed.
